audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart contradicts the packet chart and the prose: win[0]/phases[0].side said Ryze, win[1] said Skill, win[4] said Ryze (while whys[4] calls level 6 'your prime all-in'), and win[6] said Jax (while whys[6] says a two-item Ryze is unkillable and you should play safe).
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill/Jax/Jax/Jax/Jax/Jax/Ryze at 54.17% over 827 games; the existing why-text already argues that shape. Ryze has no level-1 burst (Overload 5s, Spell Flux 3.5s at rank 1 but no root without Flux), Jax owns 2-6, and a 2-item Ryze roots from 615 range without entering Counter Strike range.
audit.corrected: Rows flipped to Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Ryze in both layers, with ratings realigned (5/10, 6/10, 6/10, 6/10, 7/10, 6/10, 3/10).

audit.why: Spikes read level 2 (Empower + Leap Strike), levels 3-6 (full pattern with Counter Strike), level 6 / Trinity Force, and late two-item Ryze — all four present and matching the kit. Grandmaster's Might is 110/100/90s, so a level-6 all-in is a once-per-two-minutes commitment.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was stated only vaguely — Counter Strike does not stop Rune Prison itself, and the real cooldown gap on Rune Prison was never given.
audit.why: Rune Prison (W) is a targeted cage at 615 range on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s; it only roots when Spell Flux (E) is already on you, otherwise it slows. Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not spells, so E must be saved for the autos and the follow-up, and the trade window is the 9-11s while Rune Prison is down. Overload (Q) and Spell Flux (E) are projectiles but Jax has no blocking tool.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now names the 9.5s rank-4 Rune Prison gap as the trade window; phases[4].why keys the level-6 all-in to a whiffed Rune Prison.
